channel_tagline: The old fixes that worked before there was a $200 gadget for it.
channel_about:
Hi, I'm Walt Combs. I grew up on a family homestead where you fixed things yourself, because a repairman was a day's drive and a week's wages away.

We built things to last, wasted very little, and figured out how to solve a problem before we ever thought about paying somebody else to.

On this channel, I share the old fixes I was raised on - the ones that worked before there was a $200 gadget for every little problem in your house. Here you'll find videos about keeping a house cool or warm without a big power bill, backup power and old repair tricks, pest and cleaning fixes that don't need a store run, and the kind of practical know-how people used every day just a couple generations back.

New videos most weeks.

Subscribe if you want to learn the old ways before they're gone for good.
_channel_about_note: Structure mirrors @EliasYoderAmish's real About-tab pattern (verified via WebSearch 2026-08-03, not guessed) - first-person origin line, what that upbringing looked like in practice, 'on this channel I share...' plus a plain topic list, an upload-cadence line, a one-line subscribe pitch. Content is 100% original to Walt, not his wording - see narrator_persona._naming_note for why reusing his actual text/identity is off the table (copyright + the same impersonation risk already flagged for the name and the avatar).

speech_mannerisms: Addresses the viewer directly and personally - 'you', never 'folks' or 'one'.
Opens most videos with a plain, unhurried statement of the problem before naming the fix - no channel-intro throat-clearing.
Uses one recurring sign-off across videos for consistency, e.g. 'That's the old way. Still works.' - pick one and keep it identical video to video so it reads as a signature, not a script tic.

Occasional first-person aside grounding a step in lived habit - 'I've done it this way thirty years, never once had it fail' - only when defensible as a soft, unfalsifiable framing device, never attached to a specific fabricated fact or number.
Never uses slang, never uses corporate/marketing words ('solution', 'hack' sparingly if at all, 'optimize', 'leverage').
narrator_persona.consistency_rule: Every home-hacks script must be written in Walt's voice and mannerisms above, not written generic and voiced generic. Reuse the same sign-off line and address style across all videos on this channel so repeat viewers recognize the narrator.
